summary: Fixes a gap where the myseliasan fleet control plane undercounted a node's notifications: it only relayed events pushed live while a node's control channel was connected, so anything the node raised during a disconnect was dropped with no backfill. Node builds (mymatasan and myiotsan) now accept a since=<unix seconds> query param on GET /api/notifications that returns that node's own notifications oldest-first from that time (domain/notification.Service.ListSince, capped 500/page); the persisted notification metadata now also carries the node's stable engine id (domain/notification.OriginIDKey = "__oid") so a pulled row and a live-pushed one share one dedup key. On myseliasan, ControlServer now fires an onConnect callback the moment a node's control connection is (re)accepted, which pulls that node's notifications from the last 72 hours over the tunnel and re-ingests anything missing; a new relayed_notif dedup ledger (services.RelayDedup) makes this idempotent against events already delivered live or by an earlier replay, and an hourly job prunes ledger rows outside twice the replay window. This is scoped to all three apps together (not just myseliasan) because the parent-side replay only works against a node build new enough to serve the since= endpoint -- deploying only the myseliasan half would silently no-op the replay against every existing node.
compatibility: Backward compatible and additive. A node without the since= handling (an older mymatasan/myiotsan build) ignores the unknown query parameter and returns its normal newest-first page instead -- the replay pull for that node effectively no-ops (or, worst case, re-ingests a small overlapping window, which the dedup ledger still catches for anything with an origin id) until that node is upgraded; no existing endpoint behavior changes for a caller that never sends since=. The extra __oid metadata key is additive JSON and ignored by any existing reader of a notification's metadata. The new myseliasan relayed_notif table is created empty on first boot after upgrade via the normal auto-migrator (no explicit migration needed); it is a short-lived dedup ledger, not user-facing data, and is self-pruning. No configuration changes are required; the 72h replay window and 144h prune cutoff are fixed constants, not exposed as settings in this change.
